newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI says reviewing pre-paid card restrictions.
newsitem.headline: EMI says reviewing pre-paid card restrictions.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute (EMI) said on Tuesday that central banks were reviewing its 1994 recommendation that only credit institutions be allowed to issue pre-paid cards, or electronic purses.

The EMI said in its annual report that its 1994 recommendation was drafted when pre-paid card schemes were at a preliminary stage. Since then, electronic purse schemes had been set up in almost all European Union countries.

Central banks were currently reviewing the analysis of the effects electronic money may have on the conduct of monetary policy, stability of payment systems and financial markets as a whole, the EMI said.
Electronic purses are plastic cards with an inbuilt micro-chip which stores the electronic cash value of users' accounts and can be reloaded at special machines.
Germany's Bundesbank has occasionally voiced concern on the potential impact on monetary flows of widespread use of such cards and the risk they may carry of misuse or fraud.
